stem: A nurse reviews an order to continue subcutaneous terbutaline as maintenance tocolysis for more than 72 hours after preterm contractions have resolved. What is the nurse’s best action?

options.A: Continue the medication because prolonged maintenance tocolysis is an approved use.
options.B: Clarify the order because prolonged terbutaline tocolysis beyond 48–72 hours is not approved and carries serious maternal risks.
options.C: Increase the terbutaline dose before discharge to prevent recurrent contractions.
options.D: Teach the client to continue long-term terbutaline at home without additional review.

rationale: Terbutaline labeling contains a boxed warning that the drug has not been approved and should not be used for prolonged tocolysis beyond 48–72 hours or for maintenance tocolysis in the outpatient or home setting. Serious maternal cardiovascular and metabolic reactions, including pulmonary edema and death, have been reported.
educational_objective: Recognize the boxed warning against prolonged or maintenance terbutaline tocolysis.
source_locator: Boxed Warning—prolonged tocolysis beyond 48–72 hours and maintenance outpatient/home use
source_claim_supported: Terbutaline should not be used for prolonged tocolysis beyond 48–72 hours or maintenance outpatient/home tocolysis because of serious maternal risks.
correction_summary: Rejected the original normalization of prolonged therapy and rebuilt the item around the boxed warning.
audit_findings: The stem directly presents the prohibited prolonged-use scenario.
Independent second pass found the clarify-order action uniquely safest.
